propositions: A detached compaction sweep that dies between snapshot-write/rename and commit leaves the tracker tree dirty with untracked snapshots and tracked deletions, blocking subsequent reconverge union merges.
The compaction fold lacks crash-atomicity because snapshot-write, retire-rename, and git-commit are separate steps with no rollback; killing the worker mid-fold corrupts the shared working tree.

Crash-atomicity requires an intent journal written before mutation, ordered mutation with exception-driven rollback, and startup recovery that discriminates landed folds (clear journal) from abandoned partial folds (revert mutations and snapshot).
Recovery must distinguish transient git faults from true absence of a snapshot in HEAD to avoid misclassifying a transient failure as a landed fold and incorrectly reverting it.
Incomplete rollback (a reverse-rename fails) must retain the uncommitted snapshot as SNAPSHOT_INCONSISTENT for fsck repair rather than deleting it and losing folded events.
